s.t: Pearl Charles wrote it with a friend who’d learned ABBA’s ‘Dancing Queen’ for a wedding; she calls the result, with its ‘Dancing Queen’-style piano, “a clear homage to ABBA”.
s.src: In The Bucket Playlist: Interview with Pearl Charles
s.q: could easily be an ABBA song, with its big, singalong chorus and Dancing Queen-style piano … ‘It’s a clear homage to ABBA,’ she said. ‘It was written with a friend who’d learned Dancing Queen for a wedding, ABBA’s actually complex.

s.t: Its sunny disco masks morning-after regret: Pearl Charles has said it’s about waking after a one-night stand asking “Was that the right decision?”, with thinly veiled drug references.
s.src: Rolling Stone Australia: Pearl Charles Goes Into the Mystic
s.q: Its layers of sunny production mask bleak lyrics … “But you wake up the morning after and you’re like, ‘Oh, I don’t know about that. Was that the right decision?’ The lyrics have some thinly-veiled drug references. It’s about the morning after and the regrets.”

s.t: Bobbi Rich’s video for it apes 1970s late-night music TV like Soul Train and The Midnight Special, meant to feel like a home-taped lost episode of Top of the Pops.
s.src: DIY: Watch Pearl Charles’ ‘Only For Tonight’ video
s.q: The music video, directed by Bobbi Rich, leans into those excesses, paying a sparkly homage to the late-night musical television shows of the 70’s, from Soul Train to The Midnight Special … you’re likely to feel like you’re watching a home-taped recording of a lost episode of Top of the Pops.

f.t: Her family’s house in Joshua Tree, where she first felt drawn back to classic country, was built by the first Native American Playboy Bunny.
f.src: The Forty-Five: The Future Five – Pearl Charles
f.q: My first experiences going out there were with my family when they bought a really unique house (it was built by the first Native American Playboy Bunny) in the area about 13 years ago. That was the place where I first felt really drawn to revisit the classic country music my mom had shown me

f.t: She went to school with Billie Lourd and Lily Collins and longed to act, but her parents, including Borat director Larry Charles, made her go to college first.
f.src: Rolling Stone Australia: Pearl Charles Goes Into the Mystic
f.q: Her father, Larry Charles — who directed 2006’s Borat … I went to school with, like, Billie Lourd and Lily Collins,” … “I desperately wanted to be a professional actress and musician growing up. My parents would not let me. They were like, ‘You have to go to school. You have to go to college.

f.t: The title of her album Magic Mirror came to her in a dream, after she had asked the universe to bring her a song in her sleep.
f.src: Rolling Stone Australia: Pearl Charles Goes Into the Mystic
f.q: Charles came up with the title for Magic Mirror in a dream, after she asked the universe to bring her a song in her sleep.

f.t: At four she begged to have piano lessons like her older sister; her parents said she could if she still wanted to at five, and she did.
f.src: The Forty-Five: The Future Five – Pearl Charles
f.q: I was four years old when my older sister started piano lessons and I begged my parents to let me take lessons too. They told me if I still wanted to when I turned five they would let me, and the rest is history!

f.t: At CalArts she formed the country duo the Driftwood Singers with Christian Lee Hutson, later known for his work with Phoebe Bridgers.
f.src: Rolling Stone Australia: Pearl Charles Goes Into the Mystic
f.q: While attending Cal Arts, she formed the country duo Driftwood Singers with Christian Lee Hutson , her boyfriend at the time. … Hutson, who’s since gained recognition for his work with Phoebe Bridgers
